role: wave 8 performance: b/d capture search parameters (start DI, direction, pattern choice)

staticAnalysis.pattern: zom20b/d bodies (382 B) hold 5 copies of a 0x19-byte block at +107h,+120h,+139h(live entry),+152h,+16Bh (last truncated after 81 C7 FE 0F); EB F9 tails at +11Ah,+133h,+14Ch(live),+165h. Every 4-byte window overlapping the live loop (+147h..+14Dh) also occurs in the top copy (+152h) and in the two lower copies, so no pattern choice makes the live tail the first match in either direction: backward needs 2 searches (top decoy, then live), forward needs 3. Bytes before c0 (FF 56 D6 / 7E C1 04) break the period only below the bottom copy.
staticAnalysis.engine: repos/corewars8086-6.0.0 Cpu.int87: compares word AX then DX at ES:DI+-i, writes BX,CX at the first match, DI is NOT updated, so nobody can learn where a search hit.
staticAnalysis.direction: Forward search costs one extra charge per b/d zombie; not built.
staticAnalysis.startDI: Every top-down tail consumer (V6 family, MOV_AX_WIN, LowKey, TOM_anonymous, RW, OpcodeHunter2 decoys at FFF4h-FFFCh, zrl03/ah02 decoys at FFE8h/FFECh) competes for the topmost b/d zombie. A start at B's own load address picks the first b/d below B (same zombie as before when both are above B, P about 1/3). Captured zombies execute zombie_entry inside B's body, so [4A17h] (= B's zombie_entry) gives them the same start point with no extra instructions.

threatFindings.threat: One INT87 search can capture a zom20b/d zombie at an unknown address (pattern or direction choice)
threatFindings.evidence: static: zom20b/d dumps (period-0x19 copies, the live tail is 2nd from the top and 3rd from the bottom for every window) and Cpu.int87 (first match only, DI unchanged). Each b/d capture costs 2 backward charges or 3 forward charges.
threatFindings.impact: closes the pattern-choice and direction parts of this card

threatFindings.threat: Top-down tail consumers (MOV_AX_WIN, LowKey, TOM_anonymous) shift which of our searches hits the live tail; a start at B's own address avoids them
threatFindings.evidence: threat lth21: MOV_AX_WIN 0 (4/4 cohorts identical), LowKey 0, TOM_anonymous +0.0125; only the screen cohort s2025-2 (MOV_AX_WIN) moved (+0.133, 1 cohort).

threatFindings.threat: OpcodeHunter2 / zrl03 top-of-arena EB F9 decoys partly avoided by starting the search at B's address
threatFindings.evidence: lth21 OpcodeHunter +0.050 [-0.022,+0.122] 3/1, zrl03 +0.0625 [-0.019,+0.144] 2/0; screen fby9g s2025-10 +0.067, zrl03 +0.056. Same direction as B064/B084 (verified there for p0f), but not significant here, and it overlaps p0f13 (combo 09b1x below p0f13 alone).

threatFindings.threat: A location-based b/d start loses in V6-family crowds (multi-copy cohorts)
threatFindings.evidence: screen fby9g multi -0.031 0/2 and 09b1x multi -0.039 0/2 (same two cohorts), but threat y93aj with 2 copies x 8 cohorts: V6 -0.005 1/7, V4 +0.005, rev0self +0.0075, ALL +0.0025 n.s.

threatFindings.threat: Registered_Winners loses its [9769h]-routed b/d captures to us less often when our searches no longer start where RW's do
threatFindings.evidence: screen fby9g s2025-9 (Registered_Winners) -0.133; single cohort, no targeted job.
threatFindings.impact: unknown; worth a check if locB is ever combined

recommendation: Do not promote. locB meets the numerical screen bar (+0.0079) only barely, its threat gains (OpcodeHunter, zrl03) are the same decoy effects p0f13 already captures, and combining it with p0f13 lowered the screen (+0.0135 vs +0.0178 for p0f13 alone) with a clearly negative multi group. The b/d search parameter space looks used up: one INT87 cannot hit the live tail first in either direction, and B054/B064/B084 already cover start-DI skips and the decoy-immune window. If the coordinator wants a b/d change in the next combination, use p0f13 as it is, not locB.
